doc_basis: knowledgebase.jedox.com pages marked 'optimized for Jedox version 2026.1', fetched 2026-10-11

syntax.title: General rule form
syntax.text: Rules have the form [Target] = f[Source]. Target is an area defined by dimension elements; omit a dimension's elements to cover all of them. Rules are defined per cube.

syntax.title: Rule order / overlap
syntax.text: A rule whose target overlaps an earlier rule's target is no longer effective for the overlap; specific rules must come before general rules. Exception: CONTINUE().

syntax.title: Area
syntax.text: An area is the cross-product of element subsets from all dimensions.

syntax.title: Element reference
syntax.text: Static cell reference by element name: ['2022'].

syntax.title: OFFSET in static reference
syntax.text: ['Dim':OFFSET(-1)] returns the element offset by n positions. Only in static cell references; does not work with DCR. PALO.EOFFSET is the general form needing full context.

syntax.title: Dynamic cell reference (DCR)
syntax.text: 'Cube'['Dim':'El', ...]; cube name in single quotes before brackets (may be empty for self cube). Each item MUST name the source dimension. Dimension order irrelevant; default read element used for added dimensions. DCR does not support markers directly.

syntax.title: DCR to another database
syntax.text: 'other_database':'cube'[...] references another OLAP database (not supported by DDE).

syntax.title: Multiple target elements
syntax.text: Several elements of one dimension in curly brackets: ['Months':{'Jan','Feb','Mar'}] = ...

syntax.title: No double restriction
syntax.text: A dimension may be restricted only once per rule; ['Year':'2019','Year':'2020'] is rejected by the Rule Editor. Use one list instead.

syntax.title: Current member
syntax.text: !'DimensionName' = element of the target cell in that dimension; allowed in PALO.DATA/PALO.MARKER parameters.

syntax.title: Empty string db/cube
syntax.text: "" for <database> or <cube> means current database/cube; allowed only in PALO.DATA and PALO.MARKER, no other function.

syntax.title: Removed elements
syntax.text: Rules referencing removed elements are disabled (kept on server for manual correction).

syntax.title: Comments
syntax.text: Inline // and block /* ... */ comments; persisted with the rule.

syntax.title: null constant
syntax.text: null denotes a non-existing value; in operations treated like 0 or "", but differs in output.

syntax.title: == treats 0/null/"" equal
syntax.text: 0 == null, 0 == "" and null == "" are all true.

syntax.title: Division by zero/null
syntax.text: x/0 or 0/x = 0; x/null or null/x = null; x/x = 1 (unlike Excel #error).

syntax.title: String consolidations
syntax.text: Consolidated string elements are treated like base elements by the rules engine.

syntax.title: System cubes
syntax.text: Rules can run on data cubes and #_GROUP_CUBE_DATA, #_USER_GROUP, #_ROLE_RIGHT_OBJECT, #_USER_USER_PROPERTIES, #_GROUP_GROUP_PROPERTIES.

operators.title: eq
operators.text: Equal to (Excel uses =); only used in the IF function

operators.title: ne
operators.text: Not equal (Excel <>); only used in the IF function

prefixes.title: B:
prefixes.text: Rule applies to base cells only (base element in every dimension); consolidations aggregate rule-calculated base cells.

prefixes.title: C:
prefixes.text: Rule applies only to cells with a pure consolidated element in at least one dimension.

prefixes.title: N:
prefixes.text: Older-version form of the cell type restriction ('N: in older versions'). Exact meaning not detailed on current page.

prefixes.title: (none)
prefixes.text: Without restriction the rule applies to all cells of the target area.

control_functions.title: STET()
control_functions.text: Cell behaves as if no rule exists for it. Short form [] .

control_functions.title: CONTINUE()
control_functions.text: Rule is skipped and the search for a valid (overlapping, later) rule continues.

markers.title: When markers are needed
markers.text: In 25.x and later markers are rarely required; DDE often ignores them. Use only after a specific performance issue has been analyzed. Typically for target areas of millions of cells that cannot be reduced.

markers.title: Source marker [[ ]]
markers.text: Double brackets mark a source: ['Turnover'] = B: ABS([['Quantity']] * ['Price']) calculates only where Quantity is non-zero.

markers.title: Rule types
markers.text: Markers can be defined for B:, C: or general rules.

markers.title: Several markers
markers.text: Rule is calculated if at least one marked argument differs from 0.

markers.title: Correctness restriction
markers.text: Markers may only be used on rules that always result in 0 when all marked arguments are 0; otherwise results differ from the unmarked rule.

markers.title: PALO.MARKER
markers.text: Marker from another cube; extra marker-cube dimensions given as constants. Arguments: only constants and variables, no general expressions (e.g. no IF inside).

markers.title: Indirect marker @
markers.text: Append @PALO.MARKER(...) to a PALO.DATA expression to mark expressions.

markers.title: Markers and IF
markers.text: Both IF branches should define markers if they reference different areas; marking only one branch is not recommended.

markers.title: DCR has no marker form
markers.text: A DCR must be rewritten as explicit PALO.MARKER() for marker support.

markers.title: Engine config
markers.text: Server prefers DDE on compliant rules and ignores markers; switch code M overrides; 'engine-configuration MS' forces legacy marker engine; switch S returns to static marker processing (needs OLAP restart). Changes via Jedox Support.

markers.title: Marker computation phases
markers.text: Pre-processing after rule modification or writeback, then calculation phase.

performance.title: Count potential results
performance.text: Number of potential results (product of unrestricted dimension sizes, i.e. implicit !'Dim' occurrences) is one indicator of calculation time; restrict the target area.

performance.title: Shared dimension order
performance.text: Keep dimensions shared among cubes in the same order in every cube (DDE requires sorted processor output).

performance.title: DDE-unsupported syntax
performance.text: Not DDE: references to other OLAP databases, element variables outside cell coordinates, trig, PALO.* structure functions (except DATA/MARKER), random, date functions. Above 10,000 parameters these fall back to marker/structure engines; define markers for slow rules.

performance.title: Plan complexity
performance.text: Depends on query type, number of rules/consolidations, sub-query fragmentation from recursion, complex IFs and PALO.DATA with mapping. Planner stops at 64 nodes for recursive/chained rules.

performance.title: String rule results not cached
performance.text: String values produced by rules are not cached; can hurt repeated report refreshes and Integrator extracts.

performance.title: NOW() volatile
performance.text: NOW()-dependent results are not stored in caches.

performance.title: Structure-Driven Engine
performance.text: Evaluates cell by cell; can be slow for large areas.

performance.title: Markers rarely needed
performance.text: Do not add markers unless a specific issue is analyzed.

performance.title: Dynamic marker caveat
performance.text: Dynamic marker processing can be slower for indirect markers on aggregated cells.

performance.title: Planner constant folding
performance.text: Planner folds constants and constant IF conditions.

functions.name: ABS
functions.description: Returns the absolute value of a number. The absolute value of a number is the number without its sign.

functions.name: ACOS
functions.description: Returns the inverse cosine of a number. The returned angle is given in radians.

functions.name: ADD
functions.description: Returns the sum of its two arguments.

functions.name: AND
functions.description: Returns TRUE if all its arguments evaluate to TRUE; returns FALSE if one or more arguments evaluate to FALSE.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: ASIN
functions.description: Returns the inverse sine. The returned angle is given in radians.

functions.name: ATAN
functions.description: Returns the inverse tangent. The returned angle is given in radians.

functions.name: AVERAGE
functions.description: Returns the average of its arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: CEILING
functions.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest integer or the nearest multiple of significance.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature lists one argument but description mentions 'multiple of significance'; max_args taken from signature.

functions.name: CHAR
functions.description: Returns a character specified by a code number.

functions.name: CLEAN
functions.description: Removes all non-printable characters from the text.

functions.name: CODE
functions.description: Returns a numeric code for the first character in a text string.

functions.name: CONCATENATE
functions.description: Joins two or more text items into one text item.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: CONTINUE
functions.description: If a rule evaluates to CONTINUE then that rule is skipped and search for valid rule is continued.

functions.name: COS
functions.description: Returns the cosine. The number is given in radians.

functions.name: COUNT
functions.description: Returns the number of values provided.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: DATE
functions.description: Returns a serial number that represents a particular date based on the server rules time system . The year argument must be four digits that are greater than or equal to 1900 and smaller than or equal to 10,000. Example: Date(2015,1,1) returns 1420070400. (60*60*24*16436 seconds since 1.1.1970)."Month" is a number representing the month of the year. If Month is greater than 12, then the date will be calculated as follows: the month will be determined as Month – 12, and the year will be determined as Year + 1. For example, DATE(2008,14,2) returns the serial number 1233532800, which represents February 2, 2009."Day" is a number representing the day of the month. If Day is greater than the number of days in the month specified, then the date will be calculated as follows: the day will be determined as the excess number of days, and the month will be determined as Month + 1. For example, DATE(2008,1,35) returns the serial number 1202083200, which represents February 4, 2008.

functions.name: DATEFORMAT
functions.description: Converts a serial number date to string format, where "date" is a numeric date value (serial number) and "format" is a string with the following switches: \y Last two digits of the year (97, 98, etc) \Y Four digits of the year (1997, 1998, etc) \m Two digits of the month (01 - 12) \M Abbreviation for the month (Jan, Feb, etc) \d Two digits for the day (01 - 31) \D Digit for the day (1 - 31) \h Hour in military time (00 - 23) \H Hour in standard time (01 - 12) \i Minutes (00 - 59) \s Seconds (00 - 59) \p AM or PM Example: =DATEFORMAT(1294158800, "\Y \M \d \H \i \s \p") returns "2011 Jan 04 04 33 20 PM" (Universal Time Coordinated).
functions.return_type: Last two digits of the year (97, 98, etc)

functions.name: DATEVALUE
functions.description: Returns the serial number of the date represented as MM-DD-YYYY, MM.DD.YYYY, or MM,DD,YYYY. The function also returns correct values if the date is represented as MM-DD-YY, MM.DD.YY, or MM,DD,YY, as long as YY represents a year later than 1999.Examples:=DATEVALUE("01-02-2015") returns serial number 1420156800, which represents 02-Jan-2015 (=60*60*24*16437 seconds since 1.1.1970).=DATEVALUE("01-02-70") returns serial number 3155846400, which represents 02-Jan-2070  (=60*60*24*36526 seconds since 1.1.1970). Note that this would be an incorrect result if the intended year was 1970.

functions.name: DEL
functions.description: Returns the result of subtracting the second argument from the first.

functions.name: DIV
functions.description: Returns the result of dividing the two arguments.

functions.name: EQ
functions.description: Checks if the two arguments, which can be of type string or double, are exactly equal. Returns true or false accordingly. Both arguments must be of the same type.

functions.name: ES
functions.description: Returns the average of the values exceeding k-th percentile of values in a list, where k-th percentile is in the range 0..1 (inclusive).
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: EVEN
functions.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest even integer.

functions.name: EXACT
functions.description: Checks to see if two text values are identical. Compares two text strings and returns 1 if they are exactly the same; otherwise returns 0. This function is case-sensitive.

functions.name: EXIST
functions.description: Determines whether a cube cell holds a value or not. It returns null if x is empty, or 1 if x is numeric, string, or an error. Parameter can be numeric (including zero) or string (including empty). Note: this rule replaces ISNULL, which will be deprecated in the future.

functions.name: EXP
functions.description: Returns e raised to the power of a given number. Returns null for null input.

functions.name: FACT
functions.description: Returns the factorial of the argument. Can be slow for very large numbers.
functions.performance_note: Can be slow for very large numbers (doc).

functions.name: FIRST
functions.description: Returns first of its arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.description: Rounds a number down toward zero.

functions.name: GE
functions.description: Checks if the first argument is greater than or equal to the second argument. Both arguments must be the same type, which can be double or string.

functions.name: GT
functions.description: Checks if the first argument is greater than the second argument. Both arguments must be the same type, which can be double or string.

functions.name: IF
functions.description: Checks if the first parameter is TRUE. In this case, the second parameter is returned. Otherwise, the third parameter is returned.The third (false) argument can be omitted for OLAP rules; in this case, the default value for the third argument internally will be null. This option is also available for the graphical rule editor. To remove the third argument from the IF expression, click the cogwheel menu in the interface and select Delete.
functions.arg_note: Third argument optional for OLAP rules; defaults to null (doc).

functions.name: IFS
functions.description: Evaluates multiple expressions and returns a value that corresponds to the first TRUE result. In contrast to IFS in Excel , the number of arguments must always be even. As a workaround, a "default" result could be handled by using TRUE as the last condition argument. Note: <default> (=default result) can only be the last argument, but is optional.
functions.arg_note: Number of arguments must always be even; use TRUE as last condition for a default (doc).

functions.name: INT
functions.description: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer.

functions.name: ISERROR
functions.description: Returns TRUE if test expression can't be evaluated or evaluates to non-string or non-numeric value.

functions.name: ISNULL
functions.description: Function returns: 1 if value is null null if value is error, numeric (including 0), or string (including empty string) Note: this function has been effectively replaced by EXIST(x) and will be deprecated in the future.
functions.deprecated_note: Effectively replaced by EXIST(x); will be deprecated in the future (doc).

functions.name: LAST
functions.description: Returns last of its arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: LE
functions.description: Checks if the first argument is less than or equal to the second argument. Both arguments must have the same type, which can be double or string.

functions.name: LEFT
functions.description: Returns the leftmost characters from a text value. "text" is the text string that contains the characters you want to extract, and "num_chars" specifies the number of characters to be extracted. The value of num_chars must be greater than or equal to zero. If num_chars is greater than the length of text, LEFT returns all of the text. If num_chars is omitted, it is assumed to be 1.
functions.arg_types: text: base string num_chars: number of chars
functions.arg_note: num_chars optional, assumed 1 if omitted (doc).

functions.name: LEN
functions.description: Returns the number of characters in a text string.

functions.name: LN
functions.description: Returns the natural logarithm of a number.

functions.name: LOG
functions.description: Returns the logarithm of a number to a specified base.

functions.name: LOG10
functions.description: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number.

functions.name: LOWER
functions.description: Converts text to lowercase.

functions.name: LT
functions.description: Checks if the first argument is less than the second argument. Both arguments must have the same type, which can be double or string.

functions.name: MAX
functions.description: Returns the maximum value of the given arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: MEDIAN
functions.description: Returns the median of the given arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: MID
functions.description: Returns a specific number of characters from a text string, starting at the specified position and number of characters. "text" is the text string containing the characters you want to extract. "start_num" is the position of the first character you want to extract from the text. "num_chars" specifies the number of characters you want to return from text.Output: If start_num is greater than the length of text, MID returns null If start_num is less than the length of text, but start_num plus num_chars exceeds the length of text, MID returns the characters up to the end of text If start_num is less than 1, MID returns null If num_chars is negative, MID returns null
functions.arg_types: text: base string start_num: position num_chars: number of characters

functions.name: MIN
functions.description: Returns the minimum value of the given arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: MOD
functions.description: Returns the remainder after the number is divided by divisor. The result has the same sign as the divisor.

functions.name: MUL
functions.description: Returns the product of multiplying the two arguments.

functions.name: NE
functions.description: Checks if the two arguments, which can be of type string or double, are exactly equal. Returns true if there is no equality and false otherwise. Both arguments must be the same type.

functions.name: NOT
functions.description: Returns the logical NOT of given argument. Can be slow when negating a large, sparse data set.
functions.performance_note: Can be slow when negating a large, sparse data set (doc).

functions.name: NOW
functions.description: Returns the time when an OLAP job began processing. See note on the time system for server rules . Warning: using NOW() could slow down subsequent report calculations, because rule results that depend on the NOW() function result and other volatile data sources are not stored in cube caches.
functions.performance_note: Results depending on NOW() are not stored in cube caches; can slow later report calculations (doc).

functions.name: ODD
functions.description: Returns number rounded up to the nearest odd integer.

functions.name: OR
functions.description: Returns the logical OR of its arguments.

functions.name: PALO.CUBEDIMENSION
functions.description: Returns the name of the nth dimension in a specified hypercube.

functions.name: PALO.DATA
functions.description: Retrieves the value of the specified element from the cube.An empty string ("") can be entered for the <database> and <cube> arguments.
functions.arg_note: database, cube, then one coordinate per cube dimension. "" allowed for database/cube = current (doc).

functions.name: PALO.ECHILD
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the specified child element.
functions.arg_types: database, dimension, parent element, number of child element to retrieve

functions.name: PALO.ECHILDCOUNT
functions.description: Retrieves the number of children in the specified consolidated element.

functions.name: PALO.ECOUNT
functions.description: Retrieves the amount of dimension elements in the specified dimension.

functions.name: PALO.EFIRST
functions.description: Retrieves the first element in the specified dimension.

functions.name: PALO.EINDENT
functions.description: Retrieves the indention level of the specified element.

functions.name: PALO.EINDEX
functions.description: Retrieves the position of the specified dimension element.

functions.name: PALO.EISANC
functions.description: Checks if a consolidated element contains a specified element in all of its descendants; results in 0 or 1.Similar to PALO.EISCHILD but  also checks indirect relations between elements, e.g. Year to January, when Q1 is child of Year and Q1 is parent of January.PALO.EISANC("", "month", "Year", "January") returns 1.Function returns #ERROR when nonexistent database, dimension, or element is specified as a parameter.

functions.name: PALO.EISCHILD
functions.description: Checks if a consolidated element contains the specified element, results in 0 or 1.

functions.name: PALO.ELEVEL
functions.description: Returns the level in the dimension hierarchy of a specified element.

functions.name: PALO.ENAME
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the element at the specified position (First Position is 1).

functions.name: PALO.ENEXT
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the succeeding element of a dimension element.

functions.name: PALO.EOFFSET
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the dimension element distant by offset from specified element.
functions.arg_types: database, dimension, element, index of offset

functions.name: PALO.EPARENT
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the n-th parent of the specified element.
functions.arg_types: database, dimension, element, index of parent

functions.name: PALO.EPARENTCOUNT
functions.description: Retrieves the number of consolidated elements which contain the specified element.

functions.name: PALO.EPREV
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the preceding element of a dimension element.

functions.name: PALO.ESIBLING
functions.description: Retrieves the name of the specified sibling.
functions.arg_types: database, dimension,  element, index of sibling

functions.name: PALO.ETOPLEVEL
functions.description: Returns the level number of the highest element in the consolidation hierarchy of a dimension.

functions.name: PALO.ETYPE
functions.description: Retrieves the type of the specified element.(numeric, string, or consolidated).

functions.name: PALO.EWEIGHT
functions.description: Returns the consolidation weight of a specified component of an element.

functions.name: PALO.MARKER
functions.description: Adds marker for a slice.An empty string ("") can be entered for the <database> and <cube> arguments.
functions.arg_note: database, cube, then one coordinate per cube dimension. "" allowed for database/cube = current (doc).

functions.name: PERCENTILE
functions.description: Returns the k-th percentile of the values in a list, where k-th percentile is in the range 0..1, inclusive.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: PI
functions.description: Returns the value of pi.

functions.name: POWER
functions.description: Returns the result of a number raised to a power.As of version 2018.3, this function returns null for null input. As a workaround to obtain the result from previous versions, you can change POWER(['number'], ['power']) to POWER(['number'], ['power'] + 0)

functions.name: PROPER
functions.description: Capitalizes the first letter in a text string, as well as any other letters in the text that follow any character other than a letter. Converts all other letters to lowercase letters.

functions.name: QUOTIENT
functions.description: Returns the integer portion of a division equation.

functions.name: RAND
functions.description: Returns a random number between 0 and 1.

functions.name: RANDBETWEEN
functions.description: Returns a random number in the range you specify.

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.description: Replaces part of a text string with a different text string, based on the specified number of characters. "old_text" is the text in which you want to replace some characters. "start_num" is the position of the character in old_text that you want to replace with new_text. "num_chars" is the number of characters in old_text that you want to replace with new_text. "new_text" is the text that will replace characters in old_text.
functions.arg_types: old_text: base string start_num: start index num_chars: end index new_text: replacement

functions.name: REPT
functions.description: Repeats text a given number of times. "text" is the text you want to repeat. "num_times" is a positive number specifying the number of times to repeat text. If num_times is 0 (zero), REPT returns null. If number_times is not an integer, it is truncated.
functions.arg_types: text: base-string num_times: number of repetitions

functions.name: RIGHT
functions.description: Returns the rightmost characters from a text value. "text" is the text string that contains the characters you want to extract. "num_chars" specifies the number of characters you want to extract and must be greater than or equal to zero. If num_chars is greater than the length of text, RIGHT returns all of the text. If num_chars is omitted, it is assumed to be 1.
functions.arg_types: text: base-string num_chars: number of chars
functions.arg_note: Doc text does not state num_chars is optional; min_args=1 is by analogy to LEFT.

functions.name: ROUND
functions.description: Rounds a number to a specified number of digits. If num_digits is 0, then number is rounded to the nearest integer. If num_digits is less than 0, then number is rounded to the left of the decimal point.
functions.arg_types: num_base: number to be rounded num_digits: number of digits

functions.name: SEARCH
functions.description: Finds one text value within another (not case-sensitive). "find_text" is the text you want to find. You can use the wildcard characters question mark (?) and asterisk (*) in find_text:  question mark matches any single character; an asterisk matches any sequence of characters. If you want to find an actual question mark or asterisk, type a tilde (~) before the character. Within_text is the text in which you want to search for find_text. If find_text is not found, then 0 is returned. If found, then position is returned.
functions.arg_types: find_text: string to search for within_text: string in which you want to search for find_text

functions.name: SIGN
functions.description: Returns the sign of a number.

functions.name: SIN
functions.description: Returns the sine. The number is given in radians.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.description: Returns a positive square root.

functions.name: STET
functions.description: If a rule evaluates to STET, then the resulting cell behaves like no rule is existent for this cell.

functions.name: STR
functions.description: Converts number to string. As of 2018.3: 2nd and 3rd parameters are optional. Default is 0.
functions.arg_types: number: number to be converted width: total length of resulting string precision: number of decimal places
functions.arg_note: 2nd and 3rd parameters optional as of 2018.3, default 0 (doc).

functions.name: SUBSTITUTE
functions.description: Substitutes new text for old text in a text string. "text_base" is the text (or the reference to a cell containing text) for which you want to substitute characters. "old_text" is the text you want to replace. "new_text" is the text you want to replace old_text with.
functions.arg_types: text_base: base-string old_text: string to be replaced new_text: replacement

functions.name: SUM
functions.description: Returns sum of values provided through function arguments.
functions.arg_note: Doc signature shows two named arguments plus '...'; whether a single argument is accepted is not stated. Static checks should warn, not error.

functions.name: TAN
functions.description: Returns the tangent in radians.

functions.name: TRIM
functions.description: Removes spaces from text.

functions.name: TRUNC
functions.description: Truncates a number to an integer.

functions.name: UPPER
functions.description: Converts text to uppercase.

functions.name: VALUE
functions.description: Converts a string that represents a number to a number. Returns 0 if the conversion fails.

functions.name: VALUEDATE
functions.description: Returns a date_text for a given serial number in the format MM-DD-YY. Target area must be of type string.

functions.name: WEEKDAY
functions.description: Returns the day of the week corresponding to a date. The day is given as an integer, ranging from 1 (Sunday) to 7 (Saturday), by default.

unverified.title: Exact semantics of N: vs B:
unverified.text: Docs only say N: is the older form; equivalence to B: is not stated on the current pages.

unverified.title: Rule syntax differences in versions before 2026.1
unverified.text: The knowledgebase is published for 2026.1 only; no per-version rule-syntax matrix was found. Only explicit historic notes (N: older, POWER/STR 2018.3, markers 25.x+) are recorded.

unverified.title: Function argument limits beyond doc signatures
unverified.text: Max argument counts for variadic functions (SUM, AVERAGE, PALO.DATA ...) are not documented.
